summary.headline: Jyothy Labs Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 8.4% (down ~820 bps YoY) as gross margin dropped to 38.5% on crude-linked input inflation.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was margin-led weakness: gross margin fell 950 bps YoY to 38.5% and EBITDA margin to 8.4%, as input and packaging inflation outran price increases of roughly 3% realised in the quarter. Ex-Pril and FA, revenue grew 8.1% in value and 5.3% in volume. Fabric Care grew over 14% in value and 10% in volume, while Home Care ex-Pril grew 2.4% and Personal Care was subdued. Management said margins should recover gradually, with H2 better than H1, and that it expects double-digit revenue growth ex-Pril and FA for FY27. Segment reporting was changed to Fabric Care, Home Care and Personal Care from Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Fabric Care
segments.commentary: Value growth over 14% and volume growth 10% in Q1; detergent powders and bars grew double digits, and liquid detergents (Henko, Ujala, Mr. White, Morelight) continued high growth. Management said Fabric Care was priced up close to 5% on a portfolio basis.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Grew 2.4% YoY excluding Pril, which exited effective 31 May 2026. Exo Liquid (bioenzyme, launched 3-4 months ago) is at early scale-up; the broader Exo franchise grew mid-to-high single digits in value and double digits in volume. Household insecticides were hit by extended summer and delayed rains.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: Performance subdued in Q1 on price increases of about 9-10% and transient supply-chain disruptions; management expects recovery from Q2. Soap noodle prices have risen since June.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ex-Pril and FA: double-digit revenue growth expected; management said high-single-digit volume growth with 3-4% price.
EBITDA margins to stay under pressure through FY27 on elevated crude-linked costs; H2 expected substantially better than H1, subject to demand and commodity stability.
Margin recovery expected gradual and more meaningful from October if commodity prices stay stable; Q2 margin not expected to be materially lower than Q1.
Aim to return to historical margin levels, but management said a large part depends on crude prices.
Step up advertising and brand-building investment after A&P was moderated over recent quarters.
Total price increases since the start of the conflict about 4-4.5%, of which about 3% flowed through in Q1 and the rest in Q2.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or commissioning figures were given in the call.
Maxo incense sticks launched in July 2026 as a government-approved product; management said it is priced at par with competition.
demand_pricing: Rural demand resilient; urban demand subdued, and general trade growth muted, though ex-Pril and FA general trade was positive per the CFO.
Modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce among fastest-growing channels; e-commerce and quick commerce growing 25-30%.
Price cuts at SKU level by competition in some SKUs; company said it is at par with competition, which limited price increases to about 3% realised in Q1.
Pril exit: Henkel did not renew the agreement and the matter is before court; no sales beyond 31 May 2026.
Management said liquid detergents are now priced below powders, and premium SKUs across home care are being discounted.
Distributor stock maintained at 15-20 days; significant part of general trade sold on advance payment.

qa_highlights.question: Why is price increase only about 3% when HUL and GCPL took about 5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited competitive SKU-level price reductions; the CFO said the blended increase was about 4-4.5% in total, with Personal Care at 9-10% and other segments at 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin gap close without crude deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the goal is to return to historical margins, but much depends on crude; raw material inflation was about 15-16% and the total impact was about 9-9.5% after 3% pricing and 3-4% efficiencies and mix.

qa_highlights.question: Has general trade declined, and what is happening in quick commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: General trade was muted on urban demand, but positive ex-Pril and FA; e-commerce and quick commerce were growing 25-30% with no material assortment or pricing gaps.

qa_highlights.question: Will double-digit revenue growth return from this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the aim is double-digit growth from the current quarter, with 3-4% price and high-single-digit volume; the FY27 target excludes Pril and FA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company looking at M&A after the TTK brand sale to Wipro?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company evaluated the TTK business but did not pursue it because two divisions did not fit strategy and two overlapped; it continues to screen assets with stringent filters.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin pressure structural, and what is the path back to 18-20% EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is not a commodity business and 90% of revenue is crude-linked; it is working on diversifying away from crude-linked raw materials and expects margins to recover once crude cools.

risks_watch: Crude and packaging costs: higher-cost inventory flows through Q2, and soap noodle prices are rising from June.
Pril legal matter pending before court; Pril exit removes a revenue base that management excluded from its FY27 growth guidance.
Competitive pricing pressure in some SKUs, and a larger competitor entering dishwash.
Personal Care recovery after 9-10% price increases and supply chain disruption.
Urban demand weakness and general trade growth; Maxo incense sticks' market entry as the second organised player.
Whether A&P steps up after being cut to 6.5% of revenue from 10.8%.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic on demand and confident that margins are transitory, but evasive on the pace of recovery and on the pricing gap versus peers. Management tied the margin path to crude prices and gave no quantified Q2 margin outlook.
key_quotes: Margin recovery is therefore expected to be progressive and closely linked to top line growth.
For FY27, excluding the Pril business, we expect double -digit revenue growth.
So, I do not see a major concern in terms of going back to the historical levels if the external environment comes down a little bit.
Our business is 90% of our business is linked to crude oil prices.
So, I think all the 3 segments will perform reasonably well.
I can't tell you exactly that this is the bottom, but it is not going to be materially lower than what we have reported for quarter 1.
